newsitem.title: INDIA: News Corp's Star steps carefully on India DTH plan.
newsitem.headline: News Corp's Star steps carefully on India DTH plan.

text.p: News Corp's Asian satellite broadcaster Star TV sought on Sunday to smooth ruffled feathers in India's Information and Broadcasting Ministry over plans to introduce a direct-to-home (DTH) satellite pay channel.
Star announced its plan to launch a DTH channel last month, but an effort to test the potential size of the market last week drew criticism from Minister C.M. Ibrahim.

Star announced the opening of customer service centres in New Delhi, Bombay and Bangalore to gauge public response to Sky digital DTH television service, and according to a company statement issued on Sunday, it received an overwhelming response.

Ibrahim had warned Indians not to be influenced by advertisements by foreign-media companies offering DTH services as they need government clearance first and as yet there is no law in place covering the service.
"Thus private broadcasting, including DTH services, cannot be started unless permitted under a law by parliament," Ibrahim was quoted as saying by Saturday's edition of the Economic Times daily.
He said the government would not give licences for possession, dealing and distribution of equipment meant for receiving such services until they had been legalised.
India's government is in the process of introducing a Broadcast Bill in the current session of parliament.
The blast from Ibrahim prompted Star to clarify the legal status of its plans to launch DTH in India.

"Currently no DTH broadcaster, including Star's proposed Sky service, is required by any India law to secure a licence from any government department or agency," Sunday's statement quoting a Star spokesman said.
However, there is a legal requirement to obtain a licence from the Department of Telcommunications (DoT) for the hardware necessary to receive transmissions on the Ku-band, it said.
A dish, antennae, satellite decode or associated front-end converter are needed to for receiving Ku-band signals.
"The reception of the Sky service is dependent entirely on the issue of Ku-band licences to dealers and viewers by the DoT," the Star spokesman said.
The statement said the procedure for obtaining licences and their cost had not yet been announced, it said.
Sky TV, a multi-channel digital television service, is part of the News Corp Group.
